note.explanation: HTML is the standard language used to create web pages. You write HTML in a text editor, save the file with the .html extension, and open it in a web browser to see the page.
examples: Use a text editor such as Notepad++ to write HTML, then open the saved file in a browser.
note.checkAnswer: Save the file with the .html extension.
note.simple: HTML is the code used to build a web page. Write it in a text editor, save it as a .html file, and view it in a browser.

options: A language used to create web pages
mcqs.stem: What is HTML mainly used for?
rationales: Correct: HTML is the standard language used to create web pages.
Incorrect: A browser displays web pages; it is not HTML.
Incorrect: A text editor is a tool for writing HTML code.
Incorrect: .html is a file extension, not the language itself.
Correct: HTML was created by Tim Berners-Lee in 1991.
Incorrect: Charles Babbage is not identified as HTML's creator.
Incorrect: Bill Gates is not identified as HTML's creator.
Incorrect: Steve Jobs is not identified as HTML's creator.

mcqs.stem: Which was the very first version of HTML?
rationales: Correct: HTML 1.0 was the very first version, released in 1991.
Incorrect: HTML 2.0 came later, in 1995.
Incorrect: HTML 4.01 came later, in 1999.
Incorrect: HTML5 came much later, in 2014.

mcqs.stem: Which tool is used to write HTML code?
rationales: Correct: HTML code is written in a text editor.
Incorrect: A browser is used to view and test HTML files.
Incorrect: An extension identifies a file type but is not used to write code.
Incorrect: A website address identifies a location and is not a code-writing tool.

mcqs.stem: Which tool do you use to view and test an HTML file?
rationales: Correct: A web browser displays and lets you test HTML files.
Incorrect: A text editor is where you write the code.
Incorrect: An HTML tag is part of the code, not a viewing tool.
Incorrect: A file extension helps identify the file type but does not display it.

options: Save it without a file name
mcqs.stem: Which extension should be added to the name of an HTML file?
rationales: Correct: The .html extension helps the computer recognize the file as a web page.
Incorrect: .jpg is commonly used for image files.
Incorrect: .mp3 is commonly used for audio files.
Incorrect: The file needs a name and the correct extension to be saved properly.

options: Refresh the web page in the browser
mcqs.stem: What should you do in the browser to see changes made to an HTML file?
rationales: Correct: Refresh the web page in the browser to see the updated content.
Incorrect: Closing the editor does not update the page displayed in the browser.
Incorrect: Renaming the browser has no effect on the page content.
Incorrect: Deleting the file would remove the page rather than update it.

mcqs.stem: Which option is a web browser named in this section?
rationales: Correct: Google Chrome is listed as a common web browser.
Incorrect: Notepad++ is listed as a text editor.
Incorrect: Sublime Text is listed as a text editor.
Incorrect: Visual Studio Code is listed as a text editor.

written.text: Q8.1. What is the purpose of the `<head>` tag in HTML?
written.finalAnswer: The <head> tag contains information about the web page, such as its title.

rubric.description: State that the head contains information about the web page.
rubric.how: Explain that it holds page information rather than the main displayed content.

rubric.why: Naming the title gives a correct example of information placed in the head.

modelAnswer: The <head> tag contains information about the web page.

explain.title: What HTML is
explain.body: HTML is the standard language used to create web pages. HTML tags come together to build a web page, much like LEGO pieces come together to build a structure.

explain.title: A little HTML history
explain.body: HTML was created by Tim Berners-Lee in 1991. HTML 1.0 was the first version. The section describes later versions and identifies HTML5 (2014) as the latest version.

explain.title: Tools to get started
explain.body: A text editor is where you write HTML code. A web browser is used to view and test HTML files. Examples include Notepad++, Sublime Text, and Visual Studio Code for editors, and Chrome, Firefox, and Edge for browsers.

explain.title: Make and view a simple page
explain.body: Write the HTML code in a text editor and save it with the .html extension. Open the saved file in a browser. If you change the HTML file, refresh the browser to see the updated content.

mistakes: Saving an HTML file without the .html extension can stop the computer from recognizing it as a web page.
Using a text editor to view the page instead of opening the saved file in a web browser.
Forgetting to refresh the browser after changing the HTML file.
Leaving out requested elements or HTML tags when writing a basic page.
